Three panes over one selection. Click a node on the map and the graph expands
around it while the query rewrites itself; run a query and any node it returns
is ringed back on the map. The triples are parsed in your browser — nothing is
pre-computed and nothing is fetched from a server.

**The query box is editable.** Start from a preset or pick *Custom query*, then
edit freely and press **Run** (or Ctrl/Cmd + Enter). The full SPARQL 1.1
grammar is available — `SELECT`, `ASK`, `CONSTRUCT`, `DESCRIBE`, aggregates,
property paths, `FILTER NOT EXISTS`. You are querying the whole graph, not a
fixed result set.

```{=html}
<div class="wdn-explorer">

  <div id="wdn-map"></div>

  <div class="wdn-query">
    <div class="wdn-bar">
      <select id="preset" aria-label="Preset or custom query"></select>
      <button id="run-query" disabled>Run</button>
    </div>
    <div class="wdn-status" id="wdn-status">Starting…</div>
    <textarea id="query" spellcheck="false" aria-label="SPARQL query"></textarea>
    <div class="wdn-bar">
      <label style="font-size:12px;">
        <input type="checkbox" id="toggle-dma"> show DMA zones
      </label>
      <span class="muted" id="hit-count" style="font-size:12px;"></span>
    </div>
    <div id="results"><p class="muted">Edit the query above and press Run.
      Ctrl/Cmd + Enter works too.</p></div>
    <div class="sel-card">
      <strong>Selected:</strong> <span id="sel-node">— click a node —</span>
      <div id="sel-table" class="kv-grid"></div>
      <p class="muted" id="sel-reason" style="margin:6px 0 0;"></p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div id="wdn-graph"></div>
</div>

<script type="module" src="assets/explorer.js"></script>
```

## What the presets demonstrate

**Sensors on dead ends** joins three things that live in different places in a
conventional workflow — the sensor deployment, the network topology, and the
EPANET result — in one graph pattern.

**All four criteria satisfied** counts reified placement criteria per node.
The overlay filter is not hard-coded anywhere in the query; it is data.

**Unmonitored large mains** is the gap analysis: mains at 200 mm and above with
no monitoring station at their start node.

**Provisioning check** returns zero rows, and that is the passing result. It
asks for stations hosting a temperature-compensated sensor but no temperature
sensor. Every station has a DS18B20, so nothing comes back. Drop the probe from
a future deployment and this query surfaces it.

::: {.caveat}
The graph carries modelled state, not measurements. Pressures come from an
EPANET steady-state run at peak demand, on elevations sampled from a 30 m DEM
and a georeference solved by footprint optimisation. Treat
`wdn:modelledPressure` as what the model believes, not what a gauge would read.
:::
